content:
Just weeks after announcing a price hike for Apple Music, Apple today announced that Apple TV is also raising its prices. Apple confirmed to 9to5Mac that the Apple TV monthly fee will increase from US$12.99 to US$14.99.

The Apple One Individual plan is also raising its price.

Apple TV and Apple One price hikes

Below are the full details of the price increases:

  • Apple TV (monthly): US$14.99 (originally US$12.99)
  • Apple TV (annual): US$119 (originally US$99)
  • Apple One Individual plan: US$21.95 (originally US$19.95)

Prices for other Apple One plans remain unchanged. When Apple raised Apple Music prices last month, it also raised the prices of the Apple One Family plan and Apple One Premier plan, but did not raise the Individual plan.

New subscribers will be charged at the new price starting today. Apple says existing subscribers will be notified of the price increase about a month before being charged the new price.

Apple last raised Apple TV prices in August 2025, increasing the monthly fee from US$9.99 to US$12.99. At that time, Apple did not raise the price of the annual plan or Apple One bundles.

Apple has significantly expanded Apple TV's content lineup over the past year. Last October, Apple announced it had reached an agreement to become the exclusive broadcast partner for Formula 1 races in the United States. The F1 streaming service is included in the standard Apple TV subscription fee at no extra charge.

Earlier this year, Apple also added Major League Soccer (MLS) streaming to Apple TV at no extra charge. Previously, watching MLS required purchasing the MLS Season Pass separately.

Apple has also performed well recently thanks to the success of new shows such as the fourth season of Ted Lasso. Apple TV today premiered the second season of Dark Matter. The sixth season of Slow Horses will premiere on September 16.

What do you think of Apple TV's new price? Is US$14.99 worth it? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
